example: Invented full-participation arithmetic, not experimental results

captions.text: Two honest clients participate. Their raw examples remain local.
The server sends w = 1 to both clients. Model parameters travel; training data do not.
Each client takes two full-batch gradient steps with learning rate 0.1.
Client A: gradient −2 gives 1.20. Client B: gradient −8 gives 1.80.
The next gradients are evaluated at different local parameters: 1.20 and 1.80.
Averaging B’s three identical losses leaves the mean loss (2w − 4)².
Clients return 1.36 and 1.96. The server has not seen their raw examples.
Full participation: weights are 1/4 and 3/4. They reflect sample counts, not trust.
The new global model is 1.81. Broadcast it again and repeat until the stopping rule is met.
Keeping data local is not a privacy guarantee. This example assumes honest, synchronous clients.
